subject: Post-demo: Security onboarding / vulnerability ops checklist and pen test report request
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Byrd <tbyrd@medintegrate.com>, security@medintegrate.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Security onboarding / vulnerability ops checklist and pen test report request

Hi Tom / MedIntegrate security team —

Thanks again for your time on the product demo this morning. Quick recap and asks so we can move the security onboarding and procurement conversation forward:

- High level: MedIntegrate is evaluating Redwood for low-latency, PHI-capable inference in the clinical routing flow. We covered deployment options (Dedicated vs Private) and logging/audit surfaces.
- Immediate security asks from your side we heard: SOC 2 status, data residency and HIPAA controls, and how we handle pen test evidence.

Can you help with the following items so our Security/Legal teams can complete the risk assessment? Ideally we’d have these by end of week so we can include them in the mutual action plan (MAM):

1) SOC 2: current status (in-scope services & date of latest report)
2) HIPAA: do you require Business Associate Agreement (BAA)? Any special scoping for PHI (fields/PII) we should be aware of?
3) Pen test: last pen test date, scope (internal/external/authenticated), vendor name, and whether a redacted report can be shared with our security team.
4) Vulnerability management: your SLAs for remediation by severity, scanning cadence (authenticated scans, code scan, external), and whether you have a public disclosure policy for findings.
5) Security questionnaire: we can push our vendor questionnaire to you via DocuSign or share a Security Intake doc; which is easiest for your team?

I’ve attached a short Redwood dataflow overview and our internal scan-request template to accelerate the exchange.

Next step suggested from our side: once we receive the pen test/redacted evidence and SLA details, Redwood’s Security (Neha and Rishi copied) will review and propose a short MAM with target dates for any evidence handback and remediation commitments.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up call if useful.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Redwood-DataFlow-Overview.pdf, redwood-scan-request-template.docx
From: Tom Byrd <tbyrd@medintegrate.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medintegrate.com
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Security onboarding / vulnerability ops checklist and pen test report request

Hi Jasmine —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers below to unblock you:

- SOC 2: Type II in-scope for our hosted services; most recent report dated 2026-10-15. We can provide a redacted SOC 2 bridge letter for initial review.
- HIPAA: We are HIPAA-aware and sign BAAs for production integrations that handle PHI. PHI scoping: we limit PHI ingestion to structured clinical IDs, notes, and timestamps in the clinical routing flow — we can share the exact field map under NDA.
- Pen test: last external/authenticated test completed 2026-11-20 (vendor: BlackRockSec). We can share a redacted findings report; see attached medintegrate-202611-pt-redacted.pdf.
- Vulnerability management: typical SLAs are: critical (CVSS >=9) — remediation or mitigation plan within 7 business days; high (7-8.9) — 30 days; medium — 90 days. Scanning cadence: weekly internal authenticated scans, monthly authenticated external scans, quarterly external penetration tests. We publish a coordinated disclosure policy to partners on request.
- Security questionnaire: Emily (cc’d) owns vendor intake. We prefer the DocuSign route for legal sign-offs and can accept a secure ShareFile upload for evidence.

Emily, looping you in as the intake owner — can you confirm preferred secure upload and whether you need a standard NDA before we share the full pen test PDF?

Tom
CTO (Acting), MedIntegrate Health
tbyrd@medintegrate.com

Attachment: medintegrate-202611-pt-redacted.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Security onboarding / vulnerability ops checklist and pen test report request — internal note

Jasmine / Rishi —

Thanks for the thread. Action items & suggested asks from Redwood Security to keep procurement moving:

1) Accept the redacted pen test report for initial risk triage. Ask for a statement from MedIntegrate on whether any critical findings remain open and the expected close dates.
2) Request evidence handback for the last quarter’s authenticated scan results (CSV or PDF) and the remediation ticket list (Jira keys preferred).
3) Clarify remediation SLA applicability to third-party libraries and infra vs application code. We should accept vendor SLA (7/30/90) but ask for guaranteed mitigation plan for criticals within 7 days.
4) MAM items & timeline (draft):
   - 2027-04-14: MedIntegrate to upload redacted PT report + scan results to secure folder
   - 2027-04-18: Redwood Security to review + send any clarifying questions
   - 2027-04-25: Joint call to review findings and agree remediation owners
   - 2027-05-15: Targeted remediation completion window for high/critical items where Redwood is dependent on MedIntegrate fixes
5) Questionnaire: prefer DocuSign for legal signatures and ShareFile/Drive link for artifacts. I’ve attached the MAM template we use internally to make the dates explicit — will populate and share after the redacted report lands.

For the procurement team, add a line item that we may need a temporary Dedicated capacity for testing in a masked dataset environment depending on findings.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment: MAM-template-Redwood.pdf
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Byrd <tbyrd@medintegrate.com>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@medintegrate.com>, security@medintegrate.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Security onboarding / vulnerability ops checklist and pen test report request — next steps

Tom / Emily —

Thanks for the quick responses and the redacted report. We’ll proceed with the suggested flow:

- Please upload the medintegrate-202611-pt-redacted.pdf and last quarter’s authenticated scan output to the secure Drive link (or ShareFile) you prefer. If there’s an NDA required before the full report, we can execute our standard NDA via the DocuSign link here: https://www.docusign.com/transactions/abcdef1234567890.
- We accept the remediation SLA framework you shared; Redwood Security will expect a mitigation plan for any critical finding within 7 business days and status updates in Jira (please include ticket links).
- I’ll populate the MAM-template-Redwood.pdf with the timeline Neha suggested and send a calendar invite for the joint review call on 2027-04-25.

Two small asks to help streamline the review:
1) If you can provide a short vendor statement confirming the scope of the 2026-11 test (authenticated/external/internal) that will speed triage.
2) If PHI field mapping cannot be shared in the open, please indicate the document path and contact for secure delivery so our compliance team can validate data scope for the BAA.

Proposed next steps:
- 2027-04-14: MedIntegrate uploads artifacts
- 2027-04-18: Redwood provides initial questions
- 2027-04-25: Joint remediation review call (calendar invite to follow)

If that works I’ll update the MAM and loop in Legal for the BAA / NDA where needed. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: MAM-template-Redwood.pdf, redwood-scan-request-template.docx
